stem:
Prisha has the prime factorisation $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 5 \times 5$ and wants it in exponential form.

Which writing is correct?

options.text: Write $2 \times 5$ only, dropping the repeated factors instead of grouping them as exponents.
Start from $2^{4} \times 5^{2}$ to invent the product, as if the exponential form produced the primes.
Write $2^{4} \times 5^{2}$, grouping four factors of $2$ and two factors of $5$.
Divide the prime factors instead of multiplying them when writing the factorisation.

teacher.key_rationale: Four 2s and two 5s group as 2^4 × 5^2. Dropping repeats, reversing which form produces which, or dividing instead of multiplying miss the exponential grouping hinge.
